title: The shared header and footer stop advertising a self-owned factory
summary: The header badge and the footer columns and feature strip are the only two elements every visitor of every page sees, so they carry the strongest implicit claim on the site: that the reader is looking at a factory's own website. They still say so. This round replaces the three remaining 'Direct Factory' statements in the shared layer with the coordinated-supply wording agreed in the work order, and turns the footer's response promise into a commitment that can actually be kept while the company is being set up. The page-level factory language is out of scope here and belongs to the later rounds.
